findings.message: The acceptance criteria are not met. No test runs pause or resume while a live engine holds the lock, so the publish-without-journaling path is untested. The only no-engine test runs `pause` and checks the exit code; it never checks the journaled hold or runs `resume --hold-id` to release it. The stale/pre-hold test calls ControlInbox directly instead of the CLI and never shows that a release older than a real hold leaves that hold in place.
findings.paved_road: Add CLI tests that: (a) hold the lockfile as a fake engine, run `main(['pause'])`/`main(['resume', '--hold-id', ...])`, and assert a request file was published and no journal event was written by the CLI; (b) with no engine, run pause, read the journaled control_hold, then resume with that hold id and assert it is released; (c) show that a release with a stale lifecycle or an older hold id leaves the current hold active.

findings.message: Direct pause with no engine running has no lasting effect. `_control` journals a control_hold under the lifecycle it found or made up, then exits. The next `drain` runs `control()` in `_locked`, which builds a new inbox with a fresh uuid4 lifecycle and a new DispatchPause with hold_id=None. So a pause applied while no engine was running is silently dropped when the engine starts. For the same reason, a no-engine `resume` never touches any admission hold, and DispatchPause's release check (`request.hold_id == self.hold_id`, where self.hold_id is None) never matches. `_control` also calls the private `inbox._rehydrate_holds()` and re-assigns `inbox.lifecycle` after construction, which is the private-method routing the ticket forbids.
findings.paved_road: Have the engine's control composition rebuild the active dispatch-pause and admission-hold state from the journal (unreleased control_hold events) when it starts. Pass the lifecycle into the ControlInbox constructor instead of assigning it after construction and calling a private method. Test that a pause applied with no engine blocks the next drain's first dispatch until a matching resume.

findings.message: The red-streak hold counts the wrong failures. The ticket says the streak counts tickets going integration-red. The diff calls `self._hold.red(stem)` on rebase failures and regate failures too, so three ordinary gate or rebase failures trigger the admission hold. Also, a candidate refused for tree-hash mismatch neither resets nor advances the streak, which is fine, but no other non-integrated outcome resets it.
findings.paved_road: Call `hold.red(candidate.stem)` only on the integration_check red branch. Keep `green()` on successful integration. Add a mergequeue test showing that rebase or regate failures do not count toward K=3.

findings.message: The acceptance criterion requires proof that red-streak and tree-hash holds block the next admission through the queue, and that serialization, re-gating, integration checks and Rework unwind still work with a hold present. findings.paved_road: Build a MergeQueue with an AdmissionHold in the existing fixture repo. Drive three distinct integration-red candidates, and separately one tree-hash mismatch. Assert that the next admit blocks, that in-flight admission is not cancelled, that a matching resume unblocks it, and that Rework handoffs are still published after unwind. Replace the stale hasattr assertion with an assertion about the injected hold.

This skips the injectable clock seam, and while held it spins forever with no bound and no journaled wait. I'm not sure whether an existing seam covers this, but engine code is required to go through the seams.
